Sanborn Fire Insurance Map, Passaic (Acquackanonk Township, Clifton), Passaic County, New Jersey, additional sheets December 1916, Sheet 94, part 1 (main map)

sheet-93-1.description: Main map of sheet 93, one of two additional sheets dated December 1916 (stamped March 9, 1917) added to the Passaic series for the part of Acquackanonk Township, today Clifton, just west of the Passaic city line. Drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north toward the upper left. The part is bounded roughly by Madison Avenue on the west, Clinton Avenue and Westervelt Avenue to the north, Highland Avenue and Ward Street on the east and Clifton Boulevard along the bottom. Peach Orchard Road crosses the sheet from west to east, and Weasel Brook winds diagonally from the top centre to the lower left, where it passes a large factory complex of brick and frame buildings (block 4) near Clifton Boulevard. Most of the sheet is laid out in blocks and streets with very little building: a row of frame dwellings lines the south side of Clinton Avenue at the top, a few houses stand along De Mott Avenue, Clinton Avenue and Jewett Avenue, and scattered sheds and dwellings sit in the open land of block 214 on both sides of the brook. The Clifton Chemical Laboratory, a cluster of small frame and brick buildings near Grove Street and 3rd Street, is noted with a reference to sheet 9. Between Gregory Avenue and Peach Orchard Road a small grid of places (Home, Edward, Pleasant and Cronje) is platted but empty. South of Peach Orchard Road, 2nd and 3rd Streets and Division Street form further blocks, with a row of stuccoed frame dwellings on 2nd Street. Several streets at the top (3rd Street, Hadley Avenue) are marked not opened. Neighbouring sheets 91, 94 and 73 are indicated around the edges.
notes: Peach Orchard Road is today Paulison Avenue.
Pleasant Place is today Home Place; Cronje Place is today Parkview Terrace.
Grove (Street) is today Sylvan Avenue; Westervelt Avenue is today Westervelt Place.

Home Place north of Gregory Avenue, Edward Place, Garden Place, Division and the 2nd and 3rd Streets south of Peach Orchard Road have no modern counterpart; the area along Weasel Brook is now parkland (Weasel Brook Park).
The junction of Clinton Avenue and Westervelt Avenue lies about 12 m from its modern position and was not used as control.
The small boxed inset at the top right (an empty block corner at Clinton Avenue and 3rd Street) was not georeferenced.

map. Passaic series sheet 93, Add'l sheet Dec. 1916 (Acquackanonk Township, Clifton; today Clifton at the Passaic line). 100 ft. Peach Orchard Road (Paulison Av), Highland Av, Gregory Av, Clinton, De Mott, Madison, Hawthorne, Jewett, Westervelt Avs, Weasel Brook, Clifton Blvd. Two parts: main map, and a small boxed inset at top right (empty block corner at Clinton Av and 3rd St) left unplaced.

Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset: empty block corner at Clinton Avenue and 3rd Street (no buildings) (one junction, its centre off the image; nothing drawn but block lines; needs anchoring on 3rd Street / Clinton Avenue with px_per_ft and north_deg, or a parcel corner (step 6b)).

sheet-94-1.description: Main map of sheet 94, the second of two additional sheets dated December 1916 (stamped March 9, 1917) added to the Passaic series for the part of Acquackanonk Township, today Clifton, along the Passaic city line. Drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north toward the upper left. The part runs from Highland Avenue on the west to Sanford Street and Paulison Avenue on the east, and from 3rd Street and Cedar Street at the top down to Clifton Boulevard along the bottom. The dash-dot boundary between Passaic and Acquackanonk Township is drawn diagonally across the right half of the sheet. The northern half is a dense residential district of one- and two-storey frame dwellings with house numbers, along Burgess Place, Summer Street, 3rd Street and Highland Avenue, and on the cross streets Gregory Avenue and Center, with smaller streets such as Ward Street, Tromp Street, Sisco Place and Winter Place. A few buildings carry stucco or tile notes; nearly all are frame dwellings with outbuildings and automobile garages. South of Peach Orchard Road the land is still open: large blocks 237 and 237A to 237C between Helen Place, Mina Place, Milton Place and Sanford Street are platted but almost empty, with a handful of dwellings near Highland Avenue and Peach Orchard Road. Six-inch and eight-inch water pipes are drawn along most streets. Adjoining sheets 93, 73, 69, 59, 14, 89 and 0 are indicated around the edges, and the bottom margin shows the ends of 2nd to 5th Avenues in Passaic across Clifton Boulevard.
notes: Peach Orchard Road is today Paulison Avenue; the sheet already labels its eastern end Paulison Avenue.
Center is today Hammond Avenue; Mina Place is today Comfort Place; Milton Place is today Byron Place; Winter Place matches today's Short Street.
The Passaic / Acquackanonk Township line is drawn diagonally across the sheet.
The inset at the top right (Madison, De Mott and Clinton Avenues) is a separate part.

map. Passaic series sheet 94, Add'l sheet Dec. 1916. 100 ft. Highland, Gregory, Burgess, Sisco, Summer, Center (Hammond Av), Helen, Mina (Comfort Pl), Milton (Byron Pl), Sanford, Peach Orchard Road / Paulison Av, Clifton Blvd. Two parts: main map, and a boxed inset at top right (Madison, De Mott and Clinton Avs between 4th and 3rd Sts).

sheet-94-2.description: Boxed inset at the top right of sheet 94, an additional sheet of December 1916 in the Passaic series for Acquackanonk Township (today Clifton). It is drawn at 100 feet to an inch but turned on the page, with north close to straight up rather than toward the upper left as on the main map. The inset shows two full blocks, 213B and 213C, between 4th Street on the west and 3rd Street on the east, bounded by Madison Avenue at the top, De Mott Avenue through the middle and Clinton Avenue at the bottom. Both blocks are lined with one- and two-storey frame dwellings with house numbers on all three avenues, a few with stucco or tile notes and small automobile garages and outbuildings behind them; a henhouse stands in the rear of block 213B. Six-inch water pipes and fire hydrants are drawn along the avenues and along 4th Street. The sheet number 94, the additional-sheet date and the scale note are printed inside the inset, and adjoining sheets 75, 91, 73 and 93 are indicated on its edges. The inset lies north of the area of the main map, around the upper end of Clinton Avenue shown on sheet 93.
notes: De Mott Avenue is today Demott Avenue.
Inset turned on the page: north about 13 degrees clockwise of straight up, against about 37 degrees anticlockwise on the main map.
